chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim, the owner of the barley, from Kathir ibn Kaltham, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then Adam received from his Lord some words'
He said: 'There is no god except You, Glory be to You, O Allah, and by Your praise, I have done evil and have been unjust to myself, so forgive me, and You are the best of those who forgive.'

'There is no god except You, Glory be to You, O Allah, and by Your praise, I have done evil and have been unjust to myself, so forgive me and have mercy on me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful.'
'There is no god except You, Glory be to You, O Allah, and by Your praise, I have done evil and have been unjust to myself, so turn to me in forgiveness, for You are the Oft-Returning, the Merciful.'

And in another narration, regarding His Statement, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then Adam received from his Lord some words,' he said: 'He asked for forgiveness by the right of Muhammad, and Ali, and Al-Hasan, and Al-Husayn, and Fatima, peace be upon them.'

key_terms.أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ: the most merciful of the merciful
key_terms.ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي: I have been unjust to myself
key_terms.كَلِماتٍ: words (plural of kalimah, referring to the specific supplication)

ai.seo_question: What were the specific words Adam learned from his Lord for repentance?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the 'Kalimat' (words) Adam received for repentance, presenting three variations that highlight the attributes of Allah as the Forgiver, the Merciful, and the Accepter of Repentance. A significant alternative narration links this primordial act of repentance to the right (Haqq) of the Ahl al-Bayt, underscoring their intercessory role in Shia theology. This connection illustrates how the Prophet and Imams serve as the means through which divine mercy is accessed, a concept deeply rooted in the narrative of human fallibility and redemption.

en.hubeali: H 14920 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim the owner of the Barley, from Kaseer Bin Kalsama, who has narrated the following:

Imamasws, said, regarding the Statement of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic: “[2:37] Then Adam received (some) words from his Lord”, heasws said: ‘There is no god except Youazwj, Glory be to Youazwj our Allahazwj and by Yourazwj Praise, I have acted in an evil manner and have been unjust to myself, so Forgive me and Youazwj are the best of the Forgivers.

There is no god except You<sup>azwj</sup>. Glory be to You<sup>azwj</sup> our Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Praise. I have acted in an evil manner and have been unjust to myself, so Forgive me and be Merciful to me, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Most Merciful of the merciful ones.

There is no god except You<sup>azwj</sup>. Glory be to You<sup>azwj</sup> our Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Praise. I have acted in an evil manner and have been unjust to myself, so Turn (with Forgiveness) to me for You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Merciful Forgiver’.

And in another report regarding the Statement of the Mighty and Majestic: “[2:37] Then Adam received (some) words from his Lord”, heasws said: ‘Heas asked for (forgiveness for) the sake of Muhammadsaww, and Aliasws, and Al-Hassanasws, and Al-Husaynasws, and Fatimaasws’.
en.sarwar: 473. Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayyub Al-Khazzaaz, from Abu Baseer, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said: ‘When Ibrahim (as) saw the Kingdom of the Heavens and the earth, he (as) turned and saw a man committing adultery. So he (as) supplicated against him. He died. Then he (as) saw another one. He (as) supplicated against him, so he died as well, to the extent that he (as) saw a third one, and he (as) supplicated against him and he died too. So Allah (azwj) Revealed unto him (as): “O Ibrahim (as)! If you (as) supplicate, it would be Answered, so do not supplicate against My (azwj) servants, for if I (azwj) so Desired, I (azwj) would have never Created them. I (azwj) Created My (azwj) creation upon three categories. There is a type of servant who worships Me (azwj) and does not associate anything with Me (azwj), so I (azwj) reward him; and there is a servant who worships other than Me (azwj) so he won’t escape Me (azwj); and a servant who worships other than Me (azwj), so I (azwj) bring out from his descendants the one who would worship Me (azwj)”. Then he (as) turned, so he (as) saw a carcass on the coast of the sea, half of it was in the water and half of it in the sand.

The sea lions came and ate what was in the water, then returned and he (as) saw some of them on top of the others eating each other, and the lions of the land came and ate from it. So he (as) saw some of them on top of each other, eating each other. That surprised Ibrahim (as) from what he (as) saw, and said: “[2:260] Show me, Lord, how You will raise the dead”. How do You (azwj) Bring back that which has consumed each other’. “He replied: "Have you no faith?" He said "Yes, but just to reassure my heart”, meaning, until he (as) sees this like he sees all the things’. “Allah said, "Take four birds, draw them to you, and cut their bodies to pieces.

Scatter them over the mountain-tops”. So he (as) cut them and mixed them up just like this corpse has been mixed up inside the lion which some of them consumed the others “Scatter them over the mountain-tops then call them back. They will come swiftly to you”. So when he (as) called them over, they responded. And the mountains were ten in number’.
